shots.vo: No skill is ever wasted. Today we learn to drive the *heaviest tank* in history — the Maus.
*One hundred eighty-eight* tonnes. That is almost one hundred fifty cars.
Your seat is up front, in a separate driver’s compartment. From here you *can’t see* the turret or the crew.
Start the *1,080-horsepower* engine. But it does not turn the tracks: it spins a generator, and the current feeds *two electric motors* — one for each track.
Want to turn? One track runs slower, the other faster. Gently: the Maus does not forgive *sudden moves*.
Accelerate. In trials it reached only *thirteen* kilometres an hour. A cyclist would pass you.
A bridge ahead. Don’t drive on: it *won’t hold* the Maus. That is why it was meant to go *under water* — up to eight metres deep, breathing through a pipe.
Now the exam. An old empty car is in the way. Throttle. *Crunch.* The Maus didn’t even notice.
Of the two Maus tanks built, one survives — in a museum in *Kubinka*, Russia.
